set.body:
VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE EXEMPLAR PARITY TIER END TO END. effectagram and rMVPA agree to machine epsilon on the same estimand across 16156 entries, and the derived scores agree exactly.

02-effectagram-searchlight.R
  rdm() over 577 centres                                          1.07 s
  self-verification against a direct loop at 8 centres            max abs diff 3.33e-16
  rsa() over 577 centres                                          1.91 s

03-rmvpa-searchlight.R
  crossnobis fold construction verified as per-run means          max abs diff 0
  rMVPA native crossnobis RDM over 577 centres                    0.50 s

04-compare.R
  both arms: 577 centres, identical centre ids, identical sphere sizes, radius 11.25 mm

  [1] MATCHED ESTIMAND, cross-validated squared Euclidean RDM
      entries compared        16156   (577 centres x 28 condition pairs)
      max abs difference      1.33e-15
      centres above tolerance 0 / 577
      GATE (<= 1e-08)         PASS

      second comparison       8.88e-16, 0 / 577 above tolerance, PASS

  [2] SHARED SPEARMAN SCORE on the matched RDMs
      max abs difference      0e+00

WHY THIS IS THE MOST VALUABLE ARTEFACT IN THE REPOSITORY FOR ADOPTION. Two independent implementations, different codebases, different authors' conventions, computing the same quantity on the same real data and agreeing at 1.33e-15 over sixteen thousand entries - with the derived Spearman scores agreeing to exactly zero. That is not a similarity claim, it is an identity claim, and it is checkable by anyone in about twenty seconds.

Nothing in my review suggested building this. Five of my beads asked for a worked example on real data; none of them asked for a head-to-head against the incumbent with a numerical gate. It answers a question my review did not think to ask and that every prospective adopter will: does this give the same answer as the tool I already trust?

It also resolves, empirically, the framing question I spent the day circling. I argued the package's problem is that its documentation undersells it. This is the counter-instance to my own complaint - the strongest possible statement of what the package does, made numerically, checkable, and already in the repository.

TWO HONEST NOTES.

The README's cost claim for THIS tier is accurate - it says about 20 s total and the three scripts run in seconds. That contrasts with the error-channel arm's cost claim, which overstates by more than tenfold (bd-01KZZSREBD26E7QGPMZF6K9CTS). So the exemplar documentation is not uniformly wrong about cost; one section is right and one is stale.

On speed the incumbent is ahead on this operation: rMVPA 0.50 s against effectagram 1.07 s for the same 577-centre RDM, roughly 2x. That is worth stating plainly rather than omitting, since the exemplar exists to make an honest comparison. effectagram's argument here is not that it is faster; it is that the same number falls out of a general evidence form that also answers contrast, RSA, coupling and - uniquely - calibrated uncertainty, none of which the incumbent provides from the same object.

RECOMMENDATION: this belongs in the README and the pkgdown landing page, not only in exemplars/. It is the single most persuasive thing the project has, and today it is reachable only by someone who already cloned the repository and went looking in a subdirectory.
set.title: Verified: effectagram and rMVPA agree to 1.33e-15 on the matched estimand; surface this outside exemplars/
